beats.text: Look up on a clear day, and the sky is blue. But sunlight itself is white. So where does the blue come from?
The answer is written in the air itself. Tiny molecules of nitrogen and oxygen, far smaller than a wave of light.
When sunlight hits them, they scatter short blue wavelengths in every direction, several times more strongly than red.
That scattered blue light reaches your eyes from everywhere overhead. That is why the whole sky glows blue.
Violet is scattered even more, but there is less of it in sunlight, and your eyes are less sensitive to it.
At sunset, sunlight crosses much more air. The blue is scattered away, and the reds and oranges remain.
Dust and pollution scatter all colors equally, which is why a hazy sky looks pale and white.
So the blue sky is not a thing. It is sunlight, rearranged by the air. Thanks for watching.
